concept: A developer portfolio built as a pixel-faithful Facebook profile clone: cover photo + circular avatar, Intro/Work/Skills/Education/Social/Collaborators sidebar cards, and projects rendered as feed posts.

taste.name: Borrowed Interface
taste.trigger: When deciding how a hiring manager navigates an unknown developer's work
taste.decision: Cloned Facebook's profile shell as the portfolio layout over inventing an original one
taste.reason: Recognition beats comprehension - visitors spend zero attention learning the layout and all of it on the work; the familiarity also reads as wit

taste.name: Projects-as-Posts
taste.trigger: When presenting each project's title, blurb, stack and screenshot
taste.decision: Framed each project as a social feed post over a static project card or case-study page
taste.reason: A feed invites frictionless scrolling, so more projects actually get viewed than a gallery of equal tiles delivers

taste.name: Weight Over Size
taste.trigger: When establishing hierarchy on a page holding many projects, skills and bio blocks at once
taste.decision: Drove emphasis with font-weight (600/700) and compressed the type scale over using a tall 40px+ display scale
taste.reason: A profile is read as information, not a pitch - big headings would waste the vertical space the feed needs and break the 'real account' illusion

taste.name: System-Font, No Web Font (restraint)
taste.trigger: When choosing typography for a site whose whole premise is mimicry
taste.decision: Shipped native Segoe UI + Arial fallback and loaded NO brand/display webfont, rejecting the usual portfolio characterful typeface
taste.reason: The authenticity of the Facebook impression depends on Facebook's actual font - a designed typeface would announce 'crafted website' and puncture the illusion
